pros: Very high single-target and AoE damage alike;
Able to function with premium teammates and without — has amazing F2P options which allow her to perform even without high vertical investment;
Completely stops time during her second Ultimate, meaning you're fully invulnerable during the cast;
Summons a REALLY cool blazing sun in the sky when casting her second Ultimate. How was that necessary??
cons: About half of her damage is concentrated in her second Ultimate — backloaded damage isn't optimal for killing several groups of small enemies like in Whimpering Wastes, not to mention the timestop effect prevents the next wave from spawning leading to lots of wasted damage without proper timing;
Her Shields have next to no strength whatsoever, they only serve as a means to activate her Signature Weapon and Echo Set buffs and won't actually protect from any meaningful damage;
Very difficult to use in quickswap compositions due to Outro mechanics. While not impossible, definitely difficult to force;
Shields don't leave you immune to interruption, be wary to dodge enemy attacks so your rotation doesn't get slowed down.

review.summary: Augusta is a 5-star Electro Broadblade DPS whose focus is on dealing high Heavy Attack damage to enemies by activating a time-stop Ultimate stance where she attacks enemies in quick succession, dealing lots of damage in the blink of an eye. Much like her Electro element would suggest, in spite of wielding a heavy weapon class, Augusta is capable of unleashing many attacks in quick succession to tear down her enemies.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Augusta is a 5-star Electro Broadblade DPS whose focus is on dealing high Heavy Attack damage to enemies by activating a time-stop Ultimate stance where she attacks enemies in quick succession, dealing lots of damage in the blink of an eye. Much like her Electro element would suggest, in spite of wielding a heavy weapon class, Augusta is capable of unleashing many attacks in quick succession to tear down her enemies.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics
paragraphs: Let's get the most important abilities of Augusta out of the way first: her 3 unique resources.
The first of which is Prowess: this is her first Forte gauge used to cast Enhanced Heavy Attacks and is obtained when most of her abilities deal damage.

The second is Ascendancy: this is her second Forte gauge restored via Basic Attacks, Intro skill, her first Ultimate and her base Resonance Skill. It allows her to cast an enhanced Resonance Skill to gain her final resource, Majesty.

Majesty has 2 points, 1 of which is acquired via her Outro and the other is acquired via an enhanced Resonance Skill with full Ascendancy. When 2 points are obtained, Augusta can unleash her second Ultimate for massive damage, ending her rotation.
Therefore, Augusta's goal will be to maximize Prowess and Ascendancy generation in order to gain her Majesty stacks and finish it off with her second Ultimate.

Additionally, Augusta starts combat with 1 Majesty thanks to her second Inherent Skill which means she won't have ramp-up issues due to lacking an Outro initially. Finally, her first Inherent Skill makes it so Augusta gains a shield for 5s every 0.5s every time she deals damage, which means she will always have extra HP in that form. Even though the shield value is rather small and it doesn't stack, it does add to her sustainability.

sections.heading: Intro Skill
paragraphs: Augusta's Intro makes her restore 20% Ascendancy and full Prowess so it's definitely a must in her rotation. Aside from that, it simply deals damage and restores Concerto Energy like all other Intros.

sections.heading: How to use Prowess and restore Ascendancy
paragraphs: Augusta's Prowess mechanic allows her to use different Enhanced Heavy Attacks, triggered with different inputs. However, Uppercut, triggered by jumping with full Prowess, is not good as it sends her up into the air and Augusta rather be on the ground at all times to maximize her damage, so make sure not to accidentally use it.

More importantly however, she has a standard Heavy Attack variant which is called Backstep which she can follow with Spinslash by pressing Basic Attack shortly after, which is her standard combo. It can be done all the same by performing a Dodge Counter with full Prowess instead of a Heavy Attack.

Other than this, her base Resonance Skill restores full Prowess and her Intro Skill does also, which should be plenty in order to restore Ascendancy fully, provided her base Ultimate is used also — as it gives the 10% Ascendancy she'd be missing. It only requires using Ultimate with enough Resonance Energy, so make sure that condition is fulfilled by having enough Energy Regen. Depending on the team, anywhere between 110% and 120% Energy Regen should be enough for Augusta to function.

sections.heading: How to use Ascendancy
paragraphs: Ascendancy is used in order to perform 3 different Enhanced Resonance Skills — which are in reality all part of the same sequence. Simply press Resonance Skill with full Ascendancy then press Basic Attack or Resonance Skill 2 more times to leap into the air and plunge to restore Majesty to full. When this is performed, Augusta is ready to cast her second Ultimate. Also, don't worry about getting interrupted; if that happens, Augusta can re-cast her Enhanced Skill sequence, no problem.

sections.heading: Second Ultimate and Outro
paragraphs: By holding Ultimate with 2 stacks of Majesty, Augusta enters her Second Ultimate stance for 7s. Within this duration, time is stopped and she cannot switch out or do anything except walk, dodge, and finish her rotation with 9 swift Heavy Attacks (simply performed by spamming or holding Basic Attack), then use a finishing move by pressing Basic Attack again.

Additionally, performing this sequence of attacks gives an effect for 30s to all characters in the team called Ruler's Realm, which grants a stronger Shield to all characters who cast Intro Skill, further contributing to sustainability.

Finally, Augusta's Outro Skill allows her to give 15% DMG Amplify to any character that she outros into, which lasts the usual 14s. It also restores 1 Majesty if that character performs their own Outro skill, and gives Augusta 15% Electro DMG Bonus for her next rotation, but be careful as all of these effects expire on swap — because of this mechanic, Augusta is much less compatible with quickswapping than most other characters as the character Augusta Outros into cannot be switched out of until they can cast their own Outro skill, since it would ruin Augusta's Majesty stack generation, thus significantly slowing down her subsequent rotation.

sections.heading: Meta position & Conclusion
paragraphs: Augusta's primary selling point is her damage output. Ranking among some of the highest damaging characters in the game, Augusta is a tried-and-true DPS not unlike the current meta damage dealers. Working brilliantly with a free unit in the form of Mortefi as well as the flexible Shorekeeper, Augusta is easily accessible and performs at the level of the greatest DPS characters. If that wasn't enough, she can reach an even higher ceiling alongside her best buffer Iuno, and alongside her she's guaranteed to make clearing endgame content a breeze (if her baseline with Mortefi wasn't already more than enough anyway).

While this weapon does have ramp-up on its DEF ignore effect, it's easily the best choice for Augusta bar none, as this weapon is specialized to be used by her in order to make full use of its effect.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Augusta's best set bar none. Increases ATK and CRIT DMG by 6% and 4% for 4s respectively when a Shield is applied to the equipped character, stacking up to 5 times every 0.5s. This totals to 30% ATK and 20% CRIT DMG, which is the best set for Augusta in specific as she's the only character in the game who's able to fully stack up this effect.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: A Transform and Summon echo similar to Nightmare: Kelpie, which gives 12% Electro and 12% Heavy DMG Bonus passively in the main slot, and unconditionally summons the Echo to deal DMG whenever an Intro skill is triggered, additionally having Transform casts for extra damage. One of them is typically used at the end of a rotation, the second cast is a bit more difficult to exploit and may require quickswapping to be utilized (difficult in a team with Augusta but not impossible). The best Echo for Augusta in any situation.

recommended_endgame_stats_target: Energy Regen: 116%-125%Lower end estimated in a team with Mortefi+Shorekeeper, higher end estimated in a team with Iuno+Shorekeeper.

skill_upgrade_priority.commentary: Skill and Intro can be skipped when levelling to save on resources at a minimal damage loss.

steps: After your third character (the one Augusta has switched into) has cast their own Outro, try to cast one The False Sovereign active Echo Skill where it makes sense to do so (try to Swap Cancel an ability of your secondary character). If this isn't possible to do without losing rotation time, then do not consider doing this.
When Augusta finishes her second Ultimate attack sequence, make sure to cast one The False Sovereign active Echo Skill before immediately switching out to cast her Outro.

Augusta can cancel the endlag on the Spinslashes in her rotation. What we mean is when the damage of Spinslash has fully come out, she can immediately follow with abilities that can chain together quicker than simply letting the animation fully play out, as follows:The first Spinslash's endlag can be cancelled by her base Resonance Skill;
The second Spinslash's endlag can be cancelled by her base Ultimate.

Augusta can cancel the endlag on one of the Spinslashes in her rotation. What we mean is when the damage of the second Spinslash has fully come out, she can immediately follow with her Ultimate which can chain together quicker than simply letting the animation fully play out: hence, the second Spinslash's endlag can be cancelled by her base Ultimate.

If needed, since Augusta and her teammates have quick rotations, when playing optimally some filler attacks may need to be added depending on the team. In Augusta's case, this isn't a problem: simply go for a few normal attacks into an extra Backstep + Spinslash combo, or go for a Heavy Attack, cancel the endlag with a dash (else you would follow up with the undesirable Uppercut Heavy Attack) and then do the Backstep + Spinslash combo as normal (this second variant will be quicker).

synergies.commentary: These are the Outro buffers that pair best with Augusta. Iuno is the best by far due to her high personal damage and giving a whopping 90% DMG Amplification effect to Augusta in total, however Mortefi and Rebecca are close seconds in the Heavy DMG buffing department. Lynae may also prove more effective than those two in conjunction with Mornye as the extent of their generalist buffing potential is unparalleled.

As the two best generalist Supports by heaps and bounds, it's no surprise Shorekeeper and Verina can slot in almost any team in the game as they provide high team-wide ATK% and 15% DMG Amplify. Shorekeeper additionally provides CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG, always making her the best third slot teammate for Augusta teams, but Verina is a close, more accessible second provided Shorekeeper isn't available. Mornye may also see niche use cases alongside Lynae and Rebecca due to their synergy with Tune Rupture and Hack mechanics respectively.

example_teams.team_notes: Mornye is more niche in use, only consider her with Rebecca or Lynae on the team (for Hack and Tune Rupture synergies respectively).
